Pur U/s 279,337, 338 Ipc Cnr No.: Dlse01-00984-2018 Manish Kumar & Ors Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. 1. Manish Kumar @ Mahesh Kumar S/o Sh. Kishore Kumar H. No. 67, Block, K-Ii, Sangam Vihar New Delhi. 2. Shahjad @ Shehzad @ Shehjad S/o Khilafat R/o H. No. 1521/3, Block L- 1st Church Colony, Sangam Vihar, Delhi .....Petitioner Versus 1. Pankaj Kumar, S/o Sh. Jagat Narayan Singh R/o Vill. Pakwalia, Thana- Daraunda Siwan, Bihar. ............Driver/Respondent no. 1 2. Deepak Jain S/o Sh. Ram Murti Jain Mact No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 1 of 32 R/o C-62, Panchsheel Enclave, New Delhi. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 3. Oriental Insurance Company. F-14, & 20, C. P. Circus, Ne Delhi. on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87091513/ 1 .......Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Date of accident : 23.07.2018 Date of filing of Dar : 01.12.2018 Date of Decision : 08.05.2023.
texts.facts: 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. It may further be noted that in this case a single DAR is filed by IO instead of separate DAR for three injured persons in the same accident namely Manish Kumar, Shehzad and Shah Alam. 3. As per the facts of the case, on 23.07.2018, concerned police official on receiving DD no. 4-A reached spot of accident at M.B. Road, Lal Kuan, Near Hanuman Mandir. It was found that the injured have already been taken to unknown hospital by PCR. Further Traulla/Truck bearing no. RJ-09-GA- MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 2 of 32 8957 which was having a container loaded with it and a motorcycle bearing NO. DL-4S-BS-9967 TVS Victor, found in accidental condition. Further during investigation, injured Manish Kumar, Shehzad and Shah Alam found admitted at AIIMS Trauma Centre. Injured Shah Alam stated that at the night of 22.07.2018 he alongwith such two other friends coming from Okhla after having food and claimant no. 2 Shehzad was driving the same. When they reached such spot of accident then from Badarpur side such offending truck came in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed and hit their motorcycle. It was about 12:30 at night and somebody informed the police and they were admitted in the hospital. 4. Initially an FIR u/s. 279/337 IPC was recorded. But after investigation it was found that injuries received by claimant no. 1 Manish and claimant no. 2 Shehzad are grievous in nature. Further it is noted in charge-sheet that claimant no. 3 Shah Alam left the hospital without treatment and concerned doctor mentioned "patient absconded" and as such no MLC result received on claimant no. 3. 5. Accordingly the charge sheet u/s 279, 338 IPC filed against the R-1. Further, present DAR also filed. 6. Further as per record R-1 and R-2 appeared initially but they did not file any reply and later on stopped appearing . 7. Further as per report claimant no. 3-Shah Alam did not even appear or participated in the present claim and his presence could not be secured. Further, as a reply is filed by insurance company/R- MACT No.:1084/18 Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 3 of 32 3. It is claimed that injured side himself was traveling without valid driving license. Further, it is the case of Triple ridding and as such driver of victim side motorcycle lost control resulted into accident as such it is claimed that it is a case of own negligence. But insurance of the offending vehicle/R3 has not denied. It is further stated that it is a case of head on collusion as such in any case it is a case of contributory negligence. 9. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal on 12.04.2019: i). Relief. 10. As per record, claimant no. 2-Shehzad, examined himself in chief as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/10 relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. 11. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 12. As per record, claimant no. 1-Manish Kumar, examined himself in chief as PW-2. Such PW2 tendered his MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 4 of 32 evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW2/A. He relied upon various documents including discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-2/1 to Ex. PW-2/9 relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. 13. He was also cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 14. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioners. Further, as per record, a medical physical disability certificate, issued by Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya hospital, New Delhi dated 12.04.2022 noting the disability of the present injured/claimant no.2/Shahjad @ Shehzad as 66% regarding left lower limb. 20. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident.
texts.arguments: 18. On the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under : Issue No.1 19. Including in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 5 of 32 that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Including in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 21. It may further be noted that including in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 27. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld..Counsel for claimants that no such evidence is proved on record that there was any such contributory negligence on their part. It is further argued that even in the cross-examination of the claimant/PW-1 MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 7 of 32 & PW2, nothing fruitful could be extracted by insurance company/R-3. 28. 30 . At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 9 of 32 medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. 31.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 31.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. 31.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 31.7. Accordingly, it is presumed and held that petitioner was earning MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that there is a vagueness in the claim that he is unable to work since the accident and no supporting documents/ witness proved in this regard. It is stated that as such, only a reasonable period for loss of income be granted, if so at all. It is further argued that functional disability, if any is much lower as it physical disability is only one leg. 56. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- MACT No.:1084/18 In other matters, awarding of interest depends upon the statutory provisions mercantile usage Manish Kumar & Ors vs . Pankaj Kumar & Ors. on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87091513/ 14 and doctrine of equity. The courts have awarded the interest at different rates depending upon the MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 23 of 32 facts and circumstances of each case. Therefore, in my opinion, there cannot be any hard and fast rule in awarding interest and the award of interest is solely on the discretion of the Tribunal of the High Court as indicated above." 57. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. LIABILITY:- 59. The award amount shall be deposited with State Bank of India, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT FUND PARKING, A/c No. 35195787436, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner. 60. This court is in receipt of the orders dated 07.12.2018 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in FAO no. 842/2003 titled as Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaibir Singh & Ors whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has formulated MACAD(Motor Accident Claims Annuity Deposit Scheme) which has been made effective from 01.01.2019. "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 25 of 32 Even in the case of literate MACT No.:1084/18 Manish Kumar & Ors. Vs. Pankaj Kumar & Ors. Page No. 27 of 32 persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him.
